articles.title: Hybrid, Suture Button, and Screw Fixation for Syndesmotic Stabilization in Isolated Danis Weber Type B and C Fibular Fractures.
articles.population: Patients with isolated Danis Weber type B or C fibular fractures requiring syndesmotic stabilisation
articles.sample_size: 90 patients (Hybrid n=28, Suture Button n=31, Screw n=31)
articles.outcomes: Primary: 6-month Olerud Molander Ankle Score (OMAS). Secondary: pain score, ankle range of motion at 12 months, radiographic measurements, complications
articles.take_home: All three fixation methods produced similar ankle function scores at 6 months, with no clear winner. The suture button method showed slightly better ankle movement at 12 months compared to screw alone, though the difference was small and may not be clinically meaningful.

articles.title: The Distal Fascicle of the Anterior Inferior Tibiofibular Ligament (AITFL-df) as a Reliable Landmark for Fibular Tunnel Positioning in Anterior Talofibular Ligament Reconstruction.
articles.authors: Lian C, Wang A, Jiang D, Jiao C, Guo Q
articles.population: Patients with chronic lateral ankle instability undergoing anterior talofibular ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Accuracy and consistency of fibular tunnel position measured by fibular tunnel ratio on postoperative 3D-CT scans
articles.take_home: Using the distal fascicle of the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament as a landmark for fibular tunnel placement produces more consistent results than using the fibular obscure tubercle, especially when the fibular obscure tubercle is difficult to see. Both methods achieved similar average tunnel positions, but the new landmark approach had less variation between patients.

articles.title: Postoperative Sensory Nerve Complications Following Ankle Arthroscopy: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Clinical Course in 545 Consecutive Procedures.
articles.outcomes: Incidence of sensory nerve complications (8.4%), nerve involvement patterns, symptom resolution rates (44.4% complete resolution, 84.4% progressive improvement at mean 13 months follow-up), risk factors (smoking and surgical approach), and predictors of recovery
articles.take_home: Sensory nerve complications occur in about 1 in 12 ankle arthroscopy procedures, most commonly affecting the superficial peroneal nerve. Most patients improve over time, but complete symptom relief takes longer than previously thought, with smoking and certain surgical approaches increasing the risk.

articles.title: Does age matter? Outcomes of pilon fracture fixation in patients above and below 40 years: A comparative study.
articles.authors: El-Desouky M, Ramzy ME, Galal AA, El-Nahal AA, Maher MA, Zawam SH
articles.population: Patients with tibial pilon fractures treated with open reduction and internal fixation
articles.sample_size: 56 pilon fractures in 55 patients (35 fractures in patients under 40 years, 21 fractures in patients 40 years and older)
articles.outcomes: Fracture healing time, functional outcomes measured by AOFAS and Olerud-Molander scores, radiographic union and alignment, postoperative complication rates
articles.take_home: Age did not significantly affect healing time or functional recovery after pilon fracture surgery, with both younger and older patients achieving comparable results. Whilst older patients experienced more complications overall, all fractures healed successfully with no nonunion or implant failure in either age group.

articles.title: Passive and Dynamic Stabilizers of First Ray Alignment After TMT-I Fusion: The C1-C2 Intercuneiform Ligament and Peroneus Longus in a Sequential Cadaveric Destabilization Model.
articles.authors: Richter A, Savov P, Ettinger S, Claassen L, Yao D, Mann FE, et al.
articles.outcomes: First metatarsal movement and stability after ligament sectioning, with and without peroneus longus tendon activation
articles.take_home: In this laboratory study, the ligament that connects the first and second foot bones (C1-C2 intercuneiform ligament) and a muscle tendon on the outside of the foot (peroneus longus) help stabilize the first foot ray after fusion surgery. When these structures were damaged in the model, the first metatarsal bone became less stable, suggesting that protecting these structures during surgery might help prevent the deformity from returning.

articles.title: Minimally Invasive vs Open Lapidus Bunionectomy: 1-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes.
articles.authors: Ward LM, Voellmicke IR, Carney DD, Belayneh R, Zeng A, Thompson R, et al.
articles.population: Patients with moderate to severe hallux valgus (bunions) undergoing modified Lapidus bunionectomy
articles.sample_size: 140 patients (66 minimally invasive surgery, 74 open surgery)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes using PROMIS scores (physical function, pain interference, pain intensity, global physical health, mental health, depression), radiographic measurements (hallux valgus angle, intermetatarsal angle), computed tomography findings, and surgical complications at 1 year
articles.take_home: Both minimally invasive and open Lapidus surgery produced similar improvements in patients' pain, function and quality of life at one year, with no meaningful difference between the two approaches. Both techniques achieved good correction of the bunion, though open surgery corrected the angle more whilst minimally invasive surgery corrected the arch position more.

articles.title: De-Implementation of Routine Radiographs in the Follow-up of Wrist and Ankle Fractures in Dutch Hospitals.
articles.authors: Vuijk DA, Krijnen P, Eggebeen NJ, Schipper IB, van Bodegom-Vos L, Termaat MF
articles.population: Adults with distal radial fractures or malleolar (ankle) fractures treated at 5 hospitals in the West Netherlands
articles.sample_size: 1,497 patients (846 historical controls, 337 after dissemination, 314 after de-implementation)
articles.outcomes: Number of routine follow-up radiographs per patient, proportion of patients without routine follow-up imaging, total number of radiographs
articles.take_home: Sharing evidence from research trials and implementing targeted de-implementation strategies significantly reduced unnecessary X-rays in follow-up care for wrist and ankle fractures, without compromising safety. Both approaches substantially decreased low-value imaging in trauma care.
